## Architecture Style

**Modular Monolith — Clean Architecture per bounded context.** Each module (`Todos`, `Notifications`) is a self-contained vertical slice with its own Domain / Application / Infrastructure layers; modules communicate exclusively via asynchronous domain events (CAP + RabbitMQ outbox), never through direct project references.

## Key Patterns

- **CQRS via MediatR 12** — all writes go through `ICommand` / `ICommandHandler<T>`; all reads go through `IQuery` / `IQueryHandler<T>`. No mixed handler responsibilities.
- **Rich Domain Model (DDD)** — aggregates encapsulate invariants and raise domain events internally (e.g. `Todo.CompleteTodo()` raises `TodoCompletedEvent`). No anemic models.
- **Domain Events + CAP outbox** — cross-module async messaging via `DotNetCore.CAP` with PostgreSQL transactional outbox and RabbitMQ transport. Guarantees at-least-once delivery with no direct module coupling.
- **Hybrid data access** — EF Core 10 + Npgsql for writes and simple reads; Dapper for complex queries and reports (ADR-0002). Separate `ReadOnly` DbContext for query-side where applicable.
- **BuildingBlocks shared kernel** — CQRS base types, `BaseEntity` with domain-event raising, cache helpers, and feature-registration primitives live in `src/BuildingBlocks/` and are referenced by all modules.
- **Testcontainers for integration tests** — real PostgreSQL, Redis, and RabbitMQ containers spun up per test run; no mocked infrastructure at integration tier.
- **ArchUnit.NET architecture tests** — layer dependency rules encoded as executable tests; violations block PR merge.

## Layering Rules

**Dependency direction (innermost wins):**
```
Domain  ←  Application  ←  Infrastructure  ←  Api
```

| Rule | Detail |
|------|--------|
| Domain is framework-free | No EF attributes, no MediatR, no ASP.NET Core references in Domain layer |
| Application references Domain only | No Infrastructure types leak into Application handlers |
| Infrastructure implements Application interfaces | Repositories, CAP publishers, external services implement interfaces defined in Application |
| Api wires everything | Registers module DI, maps endpoints — no business logic |
| No direct module-to-module references | Modules reference only `Contracts` (shared event types) and `BuildingBlocks` (primitives) |
| Cross-module communication via events only | `Todos` emits events; `Notifications` subscribes — never a direct method call or project reference |
| Contracts is a stable public API | Breaking changes to `Contracts` types require an ADR and coordination across all consumers |
